entries.title: Multi-course admin navigation
entries.content:
BRS can operate as a multi-course system where staff move between course-specific and combined operational views.
An example admin system showed course-aware navigation and reporting. Dashboard and timesheet pages can expose separate course labels, course-specific summary and four-week views, and combined views. Reports can include a Course selector so staff can report on both courses together or an individual course. Course names are club configuration values and should not be treated as product knowledge, but the multi-course pattern is reusable.

entries.title: System Configuration admin variation
entries.content:
Admin access exposes configuration categories and product warnings that are hidden or blocked from read-only roles.
Admin-visible System Configuration can include feature switches and club setup categories such as course-name configuration for multi-course installations and green-fee printer module settings. The page can display product warnings when required configuration is incomplete, such as an SMS sender ID requirement when the SMS module is enabled. Specific enabled settings, club values, and warning state are instance-specific; support guidance should explain what the setting area controls and when staff should contact support for restricted or platform-level changes.

entries.title: Configure Timesheet for multi-course systems
entries.content:
Configure Timesheet manages tee time patterns across years and can support multi-course calendars.
Configure Timesheet exposes year-based setup and can display multiple configured years for editing. In a multi-course setup, the timesheet configuration supports course-aware calendar management. Support answers should describe this as the area used to set tee times and intervals for days, months, years, and course-specific schedules where applicable. Exact dates, intervals, and configured years are club setup values and should not be copied into reusable knowledge.

entries.title: Green Fee Rates advanced structure
entries.content:
Green Fee Rates define reusable rate categories and date/rule applicability for tee-time charging and booking flows.
Admin access showed that Green Fee Rates can be organized by category and sub-category, holes, start date, end date, membership-type applicability, default status, and global status. Category families can include visitor, member guest, society, corporate, complimentary, competition, resident, hotel, tour operator, voucher, and other concepts, but individual categories and prices are club-specific. Support guidance should focus on how rate definitions connect to tee sheet bookings, online booking, reporting, and membership eligibility rather than recording exact rates.

entries.title: Reservation type online booking control
entries.content:
Reservation Types can control classification, display, and whether partially booked tee times remain available to online booking channels.
Admin help text showed an Allow Online Bookings control on reservation types. This setting determines whether partially booked tee times using that reservation type can continue to accept online bookings through connected online booking channels. Reservation types also affect timesheet display, filtering, reports, and booking workflows. Exact custom types and colours are club-specific; reusable guidance should explain the control and downstream effect.

entries.title: Configured Facilities workflow
entries.content:
Facilities can manage configured non-tee-sheet resources using booking, repeat, and resource controls.
A configured Facilities module exposes bookable resources with fields for reservation name, guests, room or facility, start and end times, repeat days, and repeat weeks. Product help indicates that adding a new reservation requires all selected time slots to be free, modifying a reservation overwrites only fields entered by the user, cancelling clears reservation values, and cut/copy/paste tools can move or duplicate reservations. Resource names and actual bookings are club-specific and should be excluded from template knowledge.

entries.title: Reports course selector and Flex Points usage
entries.content:
Reports can be filtered by course and may include module-specific reports such as Full Flex Points Usage.
In a multi-course admin account, Reports included the normal start date, end date, and report type controls plus a Course selector. The report type list can vary by enabled modules and included a Full Flex Points Usage report in the observed setup. Support answers should explain that available reports depend on modules and configuration, and that course selectors allow staff to isolate or combine report data. Exact report outputs and usage values are club data.

entries.title: Member competition charging and waiting list settings
entries.content:
Member competition setup controls booking eligibility, charging, guest charging, waiting lists, and refund behavior.
Admin help text showed that member competitions can support waiting lists, competition charging, member fees, guest fees, rules for who is charged when one member books another member, refund criteria, and membership-type eligibility. These settings connect competition setup with member booking, purse/payment behavior, booking changes, and eligibility rules. Exact charges and eligibility selections are club-specific and should not be stored as template facts.
Competition charging can charge members or guests depending on setup.
Membership type eligibility controls which members can book a competition.

entries.title: Open competition course setup
entries.content:
Open competition setup defines course, dates, times, booking format, playing format, fees, mixed team rules, and online booking go-live controls.
Admin access showed Open Competition fields including course, competition date, start and end time, competition name, booking format, playing format, competition type, number of holes, member and visitor green fees, mixed member/visitor team permission, and booking available date/time. Product help indicates that reservation name matching links configured competitions to tee times, that booking and playing formats affect the booking structure, and that the go-live date/time controls online availability. Competition names, dates, fees, and actual availability are club-specific.

entries.title: Text messaging options
entries.content:
Text messaging mirrors several email audience patterns and depends on SMS module configuration and available credit.
The SMS menu can include options for texting membership types, membership groups, selected members, timesheet contacts, and general contacts, plus purchase credit. It uses similar audience concepts to email messaging but depends on SMS module setup, sender ID configuration, recipient mobile numbers, and credit. Recent message history, recipient counts, and credit balances are operational data and should not be ingested as product facts.

entries.title: Staff [redacted-name] access profile
entries.content:
A Staff [redacted-name] account can sign into the BRS admin area and view operational pages without being able to access many configuration pages.
Staff [redacted-name] users can view dashboard, timesheet, search, reports, users summary, contacts, facilities, messages, and tools index pages. Configuration pages such as system configuration details, green fee setup, competition setup, timesheet message setup, and text messaging can return a privilege warning. This access level is suitable for gathering template knowledge from visible product structure while reducing the chance of changing club setup.

entries.title: Global admin navigation
entries.content:
The main BRS admin shell exposes consistent navigation between operational areas.
Primary navigation observed across authenticated pages includes Dashboard, Timesheet, Messages, Golf Plus, Facilities, Contacts, Memberships, Users, Reports, Search, Tools, and Need Help. These links are the main orientation points for staff users moving between tee sheet operations, communication, facilities, contact records, user management, reporting, setup, and support content.

entries.title: Dashboard overview
entries.content:
The dashboard gives staff an operational overview and shortcuts into key BRS areas.
The dashboard contains tee sheet utilisation widgets with date-range controls such as today, tomorrow, and custom ranges. It summarizes bookings and golfers and separates member and visitor activity. Dashboard shortcut groups include course status, green fees, messaging, online booking links, competition links, tee time availability, golf event booking, online tee times menu, clubhouse PC login, and product/help links. These figures are club-state data and should not be used as product knowledge, but the widget structure and shortcut purposes are reusable.

entries.title: Timesheet day view
entries.content:
The timesheet day view is the main operational page for viewing and working with tee times.
The day timesheet has date navigation and alternate views including Timesheet, Summary, 4 Week, Month, and Year. The sheet displays tee-time rows with columns for holes, reservation name, reservation type, players, buggy, and information. Booking option controls allow staff to filter or prepare booking data by tee time, holes, reservation name, reservation type, players, buggies, repeat weeks, and green fee fields. The day view can include sunrise, sunset, and other timing markers and provides a print daily booking sheet link. Observed row contents, names, prices, and booking counts are club state and should not be ingested literally.

entries.title: Reservation types and booking statuses
entries.content:
Reservation types and booking statuses classify tee-time rows and bookings throughout the system.
Reservation type options can include Member, Visitor, Guest/Member, Competition, Open Competition, Society, Corporate, Team, Reserved, Reserved For Members, Reserved For Visitors, Closed, and club-defined custom types. Booking status options can include Booking Taken, Closed, Confirmed, Deposit Cleared, Deposit Paid Bank, Deposit Received, Deposit Requested, Full Payment Received, Letter Sent, Outstanding Balance, Part Payment, Provisional, and Visitor Request. These labels drive filtering, reporting, row display, and booking workflows. Custom reservation types should be treated as club-specific unless approved separately.

entries.title: Tools index
entries.content:
The Tools page is a setup and administration index that explains what each configuration area is for.
The Tools index groups setup functions into basic and additional requirements. It lists System Configuration for club parameters and feature switches, Configure Timesheet for tee times and intervals, Green Fee Rates for visitor/society/member guest categories and rates, Reservation Types for types and colours, Booking Statuses for supported statuses, Payment Methods, Contact Categories, Catering and Refreshments, No Show Reasons, Services such as buggies/caddies/club hire/room hire/trolleys/course setup, copying services/catering/green fees between years, daily timesheet titles, timesheet messages, email and letter templates, uploads for timesheets and members/contacts, membership types, legal messages, course restrictions, messaging, member casual booking rules, competitions, clubhouse PC setup, visitor/agent/tour-operator rates, day ticket rates, golf events, and competition charges.

entries.title: Reports index
entries.content:
Reports provide date-filtered operational, revenue, transaction, booking, user, contact, and playing-statistic outputs.
The Reports page has Start Date and End Date filters and a report type selector. Report categories include tee time usage, utilisation, arrivals, booking details, revenue summaries and detail, outstanding balance, revenue/rounds by green fee category, revenue by service, catering revenue, revenue by tour operator or hotel, revenue by customer contact, visitor online booking revenue, payments by payment date, payments by transaction date/time and user, booking transactions by date booked or date playing, booking counts by user or date, cancelled bookings, playing schedule/fixtures/events, caddy master report, contact details, users/members details, member playing statistics, non-member playing statistics, and contact email address reports.

entries.content:

entries.content:

entries.title: Email messaging options
entries.content:
Email messaging lets staff send targeted messages to member and contact audiences.
Email options include Email Membership Types, Email Membership Groups, Email Selected Members, Email the Timesheet, and Email Contacts. Email Membership Types can target members in a membership type and may include male/female options. Email Membership Groups targets members assigned to groups. Email Selected Members lets staff choose from a list. Email the Timesheet targets members or contacts on the timesheet for a date/time. Email Contacts targets visitors, societies, and similar contact database records. Service reminder options include Member [redacted-name] and BRS Registration Reminder. Recently sent message rows are club activity data and should not be used as template knowledge.

entries.navigationPath: Member Booking / Visitor Booking / Tee Time Availability / Open Competitions
entries.content:
BRS exposes separate online booking surfaces for members, visitors, tee time availability, tour operators, and open competitions.
Member Booking is a separate member login surface with username, password, register, forgot username, and forgot password flows. Visitor Booking explains online tee time reservation with instant on-screen and email confirmation and links to book a tee time, cancel an existing booking, and tour operator login. Tee Time Availability month view explains that each cell represents one tee time and provides a legend for free and booked reservation categories. Open Competitions explains online reservation for open competitions and instructs users to select a competition with a Book Now button when competitions exist. Club-specific visitor terms, rates, messages, phone numbers, availability, and competition lists should not be ingested literally.

MEMBER [redacted-name] Grow membership. Grow Revenue. SIGN UP FIND OUT MORE Email [redacted-email] for enquiries IN PARTNERSHIP WITH INTRODUCING OUR FINANCE PARTNER Retail finance gives customers the flexibility to buy what they really want with the option to spread the cost of their purchase of over a repayment period that suits their budget. V12 Retail Finance understand how retail finance can unlock your sales potential, and their innovative, customer [redacted-name] integrates seamlessly and will help transform your business. Working with V12 will give your customers the flexibility to choose the member [redacted-name] want with the option to spread the cost using a range of simple and straightforward finance options. BENEFITS OF MEMBER [redacted-name] GOLFERS APPLY THROUGH THE BRS GOLF MEMBERS WEBSITE AND APP APPLICATION COMPLETED IN A FEW CLICKS CLUB GETS PAID IN FULL THE NEXT DAY NO CLAW BACKS FOR NON-PAYERS PAY FOR MULTIPLE MEMBER [redacted-name] ONE GO TRACK THE WHOLE PROCESS ONLINE ABSOLUTELY NO ADMINISTRATION NEEDED BY THE CLUB SIGN UP NOW FAQs WHAT IS MEMBER [redacted-name]? BRS GOLF have teamed up V12 Retail Finance Limited (V12) to bring to you a new and flexible way for your members to pay for their golf club fees by spreading the cost across a number of payment periods to suit their budget. WHAT ARE THE BENEFITS FOR THE CLUB? BRS GOLF want to help you grow the game of golf, by increasing your member [redacted-name] and offering an alternative option to an upfront payment for golf fees. This will allow the golfer [redacted-name] the cost of their member [redacted-name] may appeal to a different sector of golfer. In addition the club will still get paid the full fees up front. NO INVOLVEMENT IN THE CREDIT APPLICATION. In working with V12 we have developed a fully-integrated solution for the finance application, meaning golfers can self-serve in applying for their member [redacted-name] through their BRS GOLF member login (desktop and/or mobile applications available). This fast, simple and secure application, makes it extremely easy for your golfers to pay for their member [redacted-name] a short on line application process - no more antiquated paper forms to hand write. Importantly, once BRS GOLF have handed the customer [redacted-name] to V12 the club members credit application is handled by V12 and the club member directly. You don't have to get involved in any sale of the finance or the legal obligations that go with it. In fact, the application for finance is so integrated we strongly believe this will increase your member [redacted-name] through this quick and popular form of payment. REDUCED RISK OF LOST FEES. Once V12 have paid you, the member [redacted-name] is between the Golfer and V12. You won't have to worry about any recourse if something goes wrong or if the golfer [redacted-name] their payment to V12. In fact, it's only in exceptional circumstances that V12 may need the clubs help to resolve member [redacted-name]. QUICK SETTLEMENT! The V12 system will provide the golfer with a quick decision within seconds of them completing their details online. Once accepted, the golfer [redacted-name] their credit agreement, the member [redacted-name] is activated immediately and you will receive payment to your bank account within 4 working days from the golfer [redacted-name] agreement. It's as quick as that. HOW DO YOU PROMOTE MEMBER [redacted-name] TO THE GOLFER? BRS GOLF will help you with advertising Member [redacted-name] to all your members (including template emails for you to send, promotional banners within your members' booking website and suggested push notifications for your app users). All financial related terms and facts will be supplied by V12. The only rule, for regulatory reasons, is that you cannot use your own credit advertisement. This benefits you in knowing that any promotion of Member [redacted-name] will be legally compliant. WHAT CAN BE INCLUDED IN THE MEMBER [redacted-name] LOAN? At the moment only the golfers playing fees can be financed this means that green fees, locker fees, buggy hire, or any other playing fees, paid for up front and spread over the term of the golfers member [redacted-name]. In the future we are working with V12 to look at adding other golfer's requirements to the member [redacted-name] so that golfers will have even more affinity with the club. WHAT DOES IT COST? The Golfer [redacted-name] charged a small administration fee on top of their loan. For this product the club won't be charged any subsidy and you will receive the full member [redacted-name]. Member [redacted-name] can be offered on 4 or 10 month terms meaning there are extremely flexible options for you to offer Member [redacted-name] to full year or partial year memberships. HOW DO WE KNOW IF A MEMBER [redacted-name] FINANCE? Through your access to the V12 system, you will have a number of helpful tools to identify which member [redacted-name] successful in their loan application, the loan amount and when this was sent to your bank account. You will also be able to run simple reports which you can download for use in your own accounting system. DO WE HAVE TO BE AUTHORISED BY THE FINANCIAL CONDUCT AUTHORITY (FCA) If you are not authorised in your own right, you can offer the interest free finance loans only, however, the agreement with V12 is that they will consider appointing the club as an Introducer Appointed Representative (IAR). As an IAR you will need to comply with V12’s specific instructions and standards for how member [redacted-name] is promoted to your members. HOW LONG DOES IT TAKE TO SIGN-UP? You will be required to provide some information to V12 directly via an online form. V12 will need to approve your application and you should be ready to go within 10 working days of V12 receiving correctly completed documentation. Once approved you will be contacted by BRS Golf and V12 with your Member [redacted-name] access rights V12 Retail Finance Limited is registered in England and Wales [redacted-number]. This will allow the golfer [redacted-name] the cost of their member [redacted-name] may appeal to a different sector of golfer. In addition the club will still get paid the full fees up front. NO INVOLVEMENT IN THE CREDIT APPLICATION. In working with V12 we have developed a fully-integrated solution for the finance application, meaning golfers can self-serve in applying for their member [redacted-name] through their BRS GOLF member login (desktop and/or mobile applications available). This fast, simple and secure application, makes it extremely easy for your golfers to pay for their member [redacted-name] a short on line application process - no more antiquated paper forms to hand write. Importantly, once BRS GOLF have handed the customer [redacted-name] to V12 the club members credit application is handled by V12 and the club member directly. You don't have to get involved in any sale of the finance or the legal obligations that go with it. In fact, the application for finance is so integrated we strongly believe this will increase your member [redacted-name] through this quick and popular form of payment. REDUCED RISK OF LOST FEES. Once V12 have paid you, the member [redacted-name] is between the Golfer and V12. You won't have to worry about any recourse if something goes wrong or if the golfer [redacted-name] their payment to V12. In fact, it's only in exceptional circumstances that V12 may need the clubs help to resolve member [redacted-name]. QUICK SETTLEMENT! The V12 system will provide the golfer with a quick decision within seconds of them completing their details online. Once accepted, the golfer [redacted-name] their credit agreement, the member [redacted-name] is activated immediately and you will receive payment to your bank account within 4 working days from the golfer [redacted-name] agreement. It's as quick as that. HOW DO YOU PROMOTE MEMBER [redacted-name] TO THE GOLFER? BRS GOLF will help you with advertising Member [redacted-name] to all your members (including template emails for you to send, promotional banners within your members' booking website and suggested push notifications for your app users). All financial related terms and facts will be supplied by V12. The only rule, for regulatory reasons, is that you cannot use your own credit advertisement. This benefits you in knowing that any promotion of Member [redacted-name] will be legally compliant. WHAT CAN BE INCLUDED IN THE MEMBER [redacted-name] LOAN? At the moment only the golfers playing fees can be financed this means that green fees, locker fees, buggy hire, or any other playing fees, paid for up front and spread over the term of the golfers member [redacted-name]. In the future we are working with V12 to look at adding other golfer's requirements to the member [redacted-name] so that golfers will have even more affinity with the club. WHAT DOES IT COST? The Golfer [redacted-name] charged a small administration fee on top of their loan. For this product the club won't be charged any subsidy and you will receive the full member [redacted-name]. Member [redacted-name] can be offered on 4 or 10 month terms meaning there are extremely flexible options for you to offer Member [redacted-name] to full year or partial year memberships. HOW DO WE KNOW IF A MEMBER [redacted-name] FINANCE? Through your access to the V12 system, you will have a number of helpful tools to identify which member [redacted-name] successful in their loan application, the loan amount and when this was sent to your bank account. You will also be able to run simple reports which you can download for use in your own accounting system. DO WE HAVE TO BE AUTHORISED BY THE FINANCIAL CONDUCT AUTHORITY (FCA) If you are not authorised in your own right, you can offer the interest free finance loans only, however, the agreement with V12 is that they will consider appointing the club as an Introducer Appointed Representative (IAR). As an IAR you will need to comply with V12’s specific instructions and standards for how member [redacted-name] is promoted to your members. HOW LONG DOES IT TAKE TO SIGN-UP? You will be required to provide some information to V12 directly via an online form. V12 will need to approve your application and you should be ready to go within 10 working days of V12 receiving correctly completed documentation. Test Test Sign Out System Tools Basic Set Up Requirements System Configuration Set up system parameters, eg. club address and email, and enable / disable certain features of the system. Configure Timesheet Set up Tee Times and Tee Time Intervals for individual days, months and years. Green Fee Rates Set up Green Fee Categories and Rates for Visitors, Societies, Member Guests, etc. Reservation Types Set up the Reservation Types and choose their colours. Booking Statuses Set up the Booking Statuses supported. Payment Methods Set up the Payment Methods supported. Contact Categories Set up the Contact Categories supported. Catering / Refreshments Set up Catering and Refreshments. No Show Reasons Set up reasons a player [redacted-name] show for a booking. Services Set up Services offered by the club such as Buggies, Caddies, Club Hire, Room Hire, Trolleys and Course Set Up. Additional Set Up Requirements Copy Services, Catering or Green Fees Copy Services, Catering or Green Fees from one year to another year. Title for Each Day Set up a title for each day of the year which is displayed at the top of the timesheet pages. Messages on the Timesheet Set up messages that get displayed on the timesheet. Email and Letter Templates Set up a number of email and letter templates for sending to members and visitors, e.g. confirmation of booking, thank you message, etc. Upload Timesheet Upload a timesheet for any given day including the player [redacted-name] member [redacted-name]. Upload Members and Contacts Upload member [redacted-name] data files into the system. Member [redacted-name] Set up member [redacted-name] such as full, 6-day, 5-day, senior, junior, honorary and country members. Legal Messages Set up Marketing Preferences, Privacy Policy, Member [redacted-name] Conditions and Visitor [redacted-name] Conditions. Course Restriction Restrict course bookings to limited group sizes. Messaging Email Messaging Send emails to your members and contacts. Text Messaging Send text messages to your members and contacts. Member [redacted-name] for Messaging Set up member [redacted-name] and assign members to those groups. Members Booking Member [redacted-name] Rules Set up the dates and times when members can view the timesheet and book casual golf on-line through the club website. Member [redacted-name] up competitions for members to book on-line through the club website. Set this PC as Club House PC Set up / remove this PC as being Club House PC. This enables certain features within the club house. Visitor [redacted-name] Fee Rates for Visitors / Agents Set up green fee rates for visitors to book on-line through the club website. It is also for setting up rates for 3rd Party Tee Time Agents. Day Ticket Rates for Visitors Set up green fee rates for visitors playing 2 rounds on the same day to book on-line through the club website. Open Competitions for Visitors Set up open competitions for visitors to book on-line through the club website. Golf Events Set up part of the timesheet for the organiser of an event to populate. This can be used for a member event, a corporate day etc. Tour Operator Booking Green Fee Rates for Tour Operator Set up green fee rates for tour operators to book on-line through the club website. Competition Charging Process Competition Charges Process competition charges for each member. Club Systems Club Systems Member [redacted-name] Maps Set up the mapping of Club Systems member [redacted-name] to BRS member [redacted-name]. Club Systems Member [redacted-name] Preview Preview Club Systems member [redacted-name] and lets you see any differences compared to member [redacted-name]. BRS Payments Payouts View Payout Schedule. FAQs Additional Help. Transactions View all transactions. Refunds View Refunds. Booking Payment Requests View the status of your Booking Payment Requests. General Payment Requests View the status of your General Payment Requests. VAT Reports Export VAT Reports. Setup Use this tool to set up BRS Payments. This benefits you in knowing that any promotion of Member [redacted-name] will be legally compliant. WHAT CAN BE INCLUDED IN THE MEMBER [redacted-name] LOAN? At the moment only the golfers playing fees can be financed this means that green fees, locker fees, buggy hire, or any other playing fees, paid for up front and spread over the term of the golfers member [redacted-name]. You will be required to provide some information to V12 directly via an online form. V12 will need to approve your application and you should be ready to go within 10 working days of V12 receiving correctly completed documentation. Facilities Contacts Memberships Users Reports Search Tools Need Help? brs chatbot Sign Out System Tools Basic Set Up Requirements System Configuration Set up system parameters, eg. club address and email, and enable / disable certain features of the system. Configure Timesheet Set up Tee Times and Tee Time Intervals for individual days, months and years. Green Fee Rates Set up Green Fee Categories and Rates for Visitors, Societies, Member Guests, etc. Reservation Types Set up the Reservation Types and choose their colours. Booking Statuses Set up the Booking Statuses supported. Payment Methods Set up the Payment Methods supported. Contact Categories Set up the Contact Categories supported. Catering / Refreshments Set up Catering and Refreshments. No Show Reasons Set up reasons a player may not show for a booking. Services Set up Services offered by the club such as Buggies, Caddies, Club Hire, Room Hire, Trolleys and Course Set Up. Additional Set Up Requirements Copy Services, Catering or Green Fees Copy Services, Catering or Green Fees from one year to another year. Title for Each Day Set up a title for each day of the year which is displayed at the top of the timesheet pages. Messages on the Timesheet Set up messages that get displayed on the timesheet. Email and Letter Templates Set up a number of email and letter templates for sending to members and visitors, e.g. confirmation of booking, thank you message, etc. Upload Timesheet Upload a timesheet for any given day including the player names and membership number. Upload Members and Contacts Upload member and contact data files into the system. Membership Types Set up membership types such as full, 6-day, 5-day, senior, junior, honorary and country members. Legal Messages Set up Marketing Preferences, Privacy Policy, Member Terms and Conditions and Visitor Terms and Conditions. Course Restriction Restrict course bookings to limited group sizes. Messaging Email Messaging Send emails to your members and contacts. Text Messaging Send text messages to your members and contacts. Membership Groups for Messaging Set up membership groups and assign members to those groups. Club News Create club news articles which can be viewed by members and the public. Club Messages Send club messages to members who are using the BRS Members App or New Members Website. Members Booking Member Casual Booking Rules Set up the dates and times when members can view the timesheet and book casual golf on-line through the club website. Member Competitions Set up competitions for members to book on-line through the club website. Set this PC as Club House PC Set up / remove this PC as being Club House PC. This enables certain features within the club house. Visitor Booking Green Fee Rates for Visitors / Agents Set up green fee rates for visitors to book on-line through the club website. It is also for setting up rates for 3rd Party Tee Time Agents. Day Ticket Rates for Visitors Set up green fee rates for visitors playing 2 rounds on the same day to book on-line through the club website. Open Competitions for Visitors Set up open competitions for visitors to book on-line through the club website. Golf Events Set up part of the timesheet for the organiser of an event to populate. This can be used for a member event, a corporate day etc. Tour Operator Booking Green Fee Rates for Tour Operator Set up green fee rates for tour operators to book on-line through the club website. Competition Charging Process Competition Charges Process competition charges for each member. Club Website Update Club Website Update Fixture List, Club News and Competition Reports on the club website. It also allows you to collect and manage member and visitor feedback. BRS Payments Payouts View Payout Schedule. FAQs Additional Help. Transactions View all transactions. Refunds View Refunds. Booking Payment Requests View the status of your Booking Payment Requests. General Payment Requests View the status of your General Payment Requests. VAT Reports Export VAT Reports. Setup Use this tool to set up BRS Payments. Help Button Launcher...... How can we help you? Facilities Contacts Memberships Users Reports Search Tools Need Help? brs chatbot Sign Out System Tools Basic Set Up Requirements System Configuration Set up system parameters, eg. club address and email, and enable / disable certain features of the system. Configure Timesheet Set up Tee Times and Tee Time Intervals for individual days, months and years. Green Fee Rates Set up Green Fee Categories and Rates for Visitors, Societies, Member Guests, etc. Reservation Types Set up the Reservation Types and choose their colours. Booking Statuses Set up the Booking Statuses supported. Payment Methods Set up the Payment Methods supported. Contact Categories Set up the Contact Categories supported. Catering / Refreshments Set up Catering and Refreshments. No Show Reasons Set up reasons a player may not show for a booking. Services Set up Services offered by the club such as Buggies, Caddies, Club Hire, Room Hire, Trolleys and Course Set Up. Additional Set Up Requirements Copy Services, Catering or Green Fees Copy Services, Catering or Green Fees from one year to another year. Title for Each Day Set up a title for each day of the year which is displayed at the top of the timesheet pages. Messages on the Timesheet Set up messages that get displayed on the timesheet. Email and Letter Templates Set up a number of email and letter templates for sending to members and visitors, e.g. confirmation of booking, thank you message, etc. Upload Timesheet Upload a timesheet for any given day including the player names and membership number. Upload Members and Contacts Upload member and contact data files into the system. Membership Types Set up membership types such as full, 6-day, 5-day, senior, junior, honorary and country members. Legal Messages Set up Marketing Preferences, Privacy Policy, Member Terms and Conditions and Visitor Terms and Conditions. Course Restriction Restrict course bookings to limited group sizes. Messaging Email Messaging Send emails to your members and contacts. Text Messaging Send text messages to your members and contacts. Membership Groups for Messaging Set up membership groups and assign members to those groups. Club News Create club news articles which can be viewed by members and the public. Club Messages Send club messages to members who are using the BRS Members App or New Members Website. Members Booking Member Casual Booking Rules Set up the dates and times when members can view the timesheet and book casual golf on-line through the club website. Member Competitions Set up competitions for members to book on-line through the club website. Set this PC as Club House PC Set up / remove this PC as being Club House PC. This enables certain features within the club house. Visitor Booking Green Fee Rates for Visitors / Agents Set up green fee rates for visitors to book on-line through the club website. It is also for setting up rates for 3rd Party Tee Time Agents. Day Ticket Rates for Visitors Set up green fee rates for visitors playing 2 rounds on the same day to book on-line through the club website. Open Competitions for Visitors Set up open competitions for visitors to book on-line through the club website. Golf Events Set up part of the timesheet for the organiser of an event to populate. This can be used for a member event, a corporate day etc. Tour Operator Booking Green Fee Rates for Tour Operator Set up green fee rates for tour operators to book on-line through the club website. Competition Charging Process Competition Charges Process competition charges for each member. Club Website Update Club Website Update Fixture List, Club News and Competition Reports on the club website. It also allows you to collect and manage member and visitor feedback. entries.navigationPath: Terms and Conditions - All Ireland Open Competitions Search Facility
entries.content:
Terms and Conditions - All Ireland Open Competitions Search Facility
Workflow: Terms and Conditions - All Ireland Open Competitions Search Facility
Step 1: Open "Terms and Conditions - All Ireland Open Competitions Search Facility" from terms and conditions php.
Step 2: Use the confirmed fields/filters on this screen: "Your club name:", "Your username:", "Please specify your name:", "Please specify your email address:", "I have read and accept these terms and conditions:", "terms_and_conditions", "query".
Step 3: Use the confirmed actions on this screen as needed: "Submit", "Dashboard", "Timesheet", "Messages", "Golf Plus New!", "Facilities", "Contacts", "Memberships", "Users", "Reports", "Search", "Tools", "Need Help?".
Step 4: Check the result table columns: "Terms and Conditions - All Ireland Open Competitions Search Facility", "Please read the following Terms and Conditions carefully before opting in to the opencomps:", "Terms and Conditions for using the BRS Golf All Ireland Open Competitions Search Facility These terms and conditions should be read in conjunction with the Information Sheet titled 'All Ireland Open Competition Search Facility'. If you do not have a copy of this please contact us by email on [redacted-email]. 1. Displaying Open Competitions on the Central Search The Golf Club agrees that all open competitions set up in the BRS Tee Time Manager can be displayed in the Open Competition Central Search Facility. This includes all information related to the open competition such as name of competition, date, course, start time, end time, tee times, number of slots booked/free, member and visitor green fees, scoring method, type of competition and when the competition goes live. The Golf Club is responsible for the accuracy of the information set up in relation to each open competition. Golfers from any club may perform searches on these competitions and shall be able to book a tee time once it goes live. 2. Updating Competition Listings BRS Golf shall update the competition listings on the central search facility at least once every 24 hours which means any new competitions added in the BRS Tee Time Manager may take up to 24 hours to appear in the search results. 3. Displaying Information on Members Booking Pages The Golf Club agrees that BRS Golf may place a graphical image and button on several members booking pages promoting the new facility to its members. Your members will then find out about other open competitions in other clubs. Similarly, all the members of all the other participating clubs will find out about your open competitions. This should boost participation and revenue generation for all clubs. Please note that BRS Golf will not display this information on Visitor Booking and Open Competition pages. 4. Duration of Contract The initial period of this contract will be from the date signed up to and including the 31st December 2012. The club can terminate this contract at any time with just 1 weeks notice. 5. Technical Support Telephone and email support will be provided free of charge. Telephone support shall be provided 9am - 5.30pm 5 days per week. The support contact number is published in BRS Tee Time Manager. A telephone answering service is provided when the support line is busy. The support email address is [redacted-email]. Email queries will normally be responded to within 24 hours. 6. Fees and Payments 2012 BRS Golf are doing an introductory offer and making this facility completely free of charge to all BRS customers and their members up to the end of 2012. This offer only applies to clubs that have paid an annual fee for the Visitor Booking Module. 7. Fees and Payments 2013 From the 1st January 2013, BRS Golf will apply a booking fee for each booking made through the search facility. All clubs will be informed in writing before any fee is applied. 8. Order Confirmation Please complete the form below, select the acceptance check box and then hit the submit button. We would like to participate in the Open Competition Central Search Facility and agree to the above Terms and Conditions.", "Your club name:", "Your username:", "Please specify your name:", "Please specify your email address:", "I have read and accept these terms and conditions:".

Action: System Configuration Set up system parameters, eg. club address and email, and enable / disable certain features of the system.: action
Action: Configure Timesheet Set up Tee Times and Tee Time Intervals for individual days, months and years.: action
Action: Green Fee Rates Set up Green Fee Categories and Rates for Visitors, Societies, Member Guests, etc.: action
Action: Reservation Types Set up the Reservation Types and choose their colours.: action
Action: Booking Statuses Set up the Booking Statuses supported.: action
Action: Payment Methods Set up the Payment Methods supported.: action
Action: Contact Categories Set up the Contact Categories supported.: action
Action: Catering / Refreshments Set up Catering and Refreshments.: action
Action: No Show Reasons Set up reasons a player may not show for a booking.: action
Action: Services Set up Services offered by the club such as Buggies, Caddies, Club Hire, Room Hire, Trolleys and Course Set Up.: action
Action: Copy Services, Catering or Green Fees Copy Services, Catering or Green Fees from one year to another year.: action
Action: Title for Each Day Set up a title for each day of the year which is displayed at the top of the timesheet pages.: action
Action: Messages on the Timesheet Set up messages that get displayed on the timesheet.: action
Action: Email and Letter Templates Set up a number of email and letter templates for sending to members and visitors, e.g. confirmation of booking, thank you message, etc.: action
Action: Upload Timesheet Upload a timesheet for any given day including the player names and membership number.: action
Action: Upload Members and Contacts Upload member and contact data files into the system.: action
Action: Membership Types Set up membership types such as full, 6-day, 5-day, senior, junior, honorary and country members.: action
Action: Legal Messages Set up Marketing Preferences, Privacy Policy, Member Terms and Conditions and Visitor Terms and Conditions.: action
Action: Course Restriction Restrict course bookings to limited group sizes.: action
Action: Email Messaging Send emails to your members and contacts.: action
Action: Text Messaging Send text messages to your members and contacts.: action
Action: Membership Groups for Messaging Set up membership groups and assign members to those groups.: action
Action: Club News Create club news articles which can be viewed by members and the public.: open/run
Action: Club Messages Send club messages to members who are using the BRS Members App or New Members Website.: action
Action: Member Casual Booking Rules Set up the dates and times when members can view the timesheet and book casual golf on-line through the club website.: open/run
Action: Member Competitions Set up competitions for members to book on-line through the club website.: action
Action: Set this PC as Club House PC Set up / remove this PC as being Club House PC. This enables certain features within the club house.: action
Action: Green Fee Rates for Visitors / Agents Set up green fee rates for visitors to book on-line through the club website. It is also for setting up rates for 3rd Party Tee Time Agents.: action
Action: Day Ticket Rates for Visitors Set up green fee rates for visitors playing 2 rounds on the same day to book on-line through the club website.: action
Action: Open Competitions for Visitors Set up open competitions for visitors to book on-line through the club website.: open/run
Action: Golf Events Set up part of the timesheet for the organiser of an event to populate. This can be used for a member event, a corporate day etc.: action
Action: Green Fee Rates for Tour Operator Set up green fee rates for tour operators to book on-line through the club website.: action
Action: Process Competition Charges Process competition charges for each member.: action
Action: Update Club Website Update Fixture List, Club News and Competition Reports on the club website. It also allows you to collect and manage member and visitor feedback.: open/run
Action: Payouts View Payout Schedule.: open/run
Action: FAQs Additional Help.: action
Action: Transactions View all transactions.: open/run
Action: Refunds View Refunds.: open/run
Action: Booking Payment Requests View the status of your Booking Payment Requests.: open/run
Action: General Payment Requests View the status of your General Payment Requests.: open/run
Action: VAT Reports Export VAT Reports.: download/export
Action: Setup Use this tool to set up BRS Payments.: action

entries.title: Demo explored workflow routes
entries.content:
Workflow routes collected from a controlled demo exploration. Review before approving for chatbot use.
Workflow: How do I add a single tee time booking?
Route 1: Admin timesheet booking route
Route 1 actor: Admin or staff user
Route 1 preconditions: User is signed into the demo BRS admin area.; A tee time row is available on the Timesheet day view.
Route 1 step 1: Open the Timesheet day view.
Route 1 step 2: Open a tee time row or existing booking from the Timesheet.
Route 1 step 3: Open the booking surface using https://www.facebook.com/BRSGOLF/.
Route 1 step 4: Use the visible booking controls and service/buggy controls shown on the booking page.
Route 1 step 5: Keep the demo booking as a draft unless commit mode is explicitly enabled.
Route 1 outcome: Booking-linked evidence is collected without submitting a booking.
Route 1 verification: Return to the Timesheet day view and check the booking row evidence.
Route 2: Online member or visitor request route
Route 2 actor: Member or visitor, where club setup allows online buggy booking
Route 2 preconditions: Club configuration permits the member or visitor channel to request buggies online.
Route 2 step 1: Member or visitor requests the buggy during the online booking journey.
Route 2 step 2: Admin verifies the request on the Timesheet booking row or booking details.
Route 2 step 3: Admin adds or confirms any service/charge required for the buggy from the booking details/service area.
Route 2 outcome: The online request appears operationally on the admin timesheet, but charging/service completion remains an admin-controlled check.
Route 2 verification: Check Timesheet booking details and service/charge controls before confirming the customer has been charged.

entries.title: Observed workflow: create membership bills
entries.content:
Reviewed demo evidence for creating subscription, renewal, batch, or all-member membership bills from Billing/Payments. No live member names, amounts, payment references, or club-specific values were recorded.
Workflow: Create membership bills
Aliases: How do I create a bill?; How do I create a membership bill?; How do I add a bill for a member?; How do I raise an invoice?; How do I create batch bills?
Route 1: Create bills from Memberships Billing/Payments
Route 1 actor: Golf club admin or membership staff user
Route 1 preconditions: The staff user has access to Memberships.; The club knows the bill reference, due date, billing period, audience, subscriptions or custom line items, and whether payment schemes should be offered.
Route 1 step 1: Open Memberships.
Route 1 step 2: Open Billing/Payments.
Route 1 step 3: Click CREATE BILLS.
Route 1 step 4: In Enter Billing Details, enter the Billing Reference and Due Date.
Route 1 step 5: Click SET BILL FILTERS and choose the bill cycle or period option.
Route 1 step 6: Use Who To Bill to confirm the members or audience for the bill.
Route 1 step 7: Select the subscriptions, discounts, and any custom bill items needed.
Route 1 step 8: Use ADD ITEM only when the club needs an extra one-off line item.
Route 1 step 9: In Payment Schemes, select a scheme only if members should be offered scheduled or instalment payments.
Route 1 step 10: Click PREVIEW and review the bill before finalising.
Route 1 outcome: The bill is prepared through the create bills wizard and reviewed before finalisation.
Route 1 verification: Return to Billing/Payments.; Use View All Bills or the bill search/filter controls.; Confirm the bill appears with the correct member or audience, due date, amount, payment status, and publish status.

entries.title: Observed workflow: create or edit a flexible membership type
entries.navigationPath: Memberships > Membership Types > CREATE MEMBERSHIP TYPE
entries.content:
Reviewed demo evidence for creating and inspecting a flexible membership type in the embedded Memberships app. Flexible membership type setup belongs in Membership Types. Member profiles are used later to assign or review an existing type for one member.
Workflow: Create or edit a flexible membership type
Workflow family: Membership type setup
Aliases: How do I create a flexible membership type?; How do I create a flexi membership type?; How do I add a flexible membership?; How do I set up a flex membership type?; How do I make a membership type flexible?; How do I edit a flexi membership type?
Variant 1: Managing one flexible member
Variant 1 applies when: The user asks about one member's flexible membership, points, balance, top-up, clawback, or account balance.
Variant 1 answer impact: Use Members to open the member profile and Account Balances for wallet movement. Do not use the create membership type route as the main answer.
Variant 2: Flexible wallets dashboard visibility
Variant 2 applies when: The user asks why flexible wallets are or are not shown on the Memberships Dashboard.
Variant 2 answer impact: Use Memberships > Settings > General and the Display Flexible Wallets table on dashboard checkbox.
Variant 3: Wallet/account setup
Variant 3 applies when: The user asks about configuring wallets, account units, auto assignment, active state, or minimum balance.
Variant 3 answer impact: Use Memberships > Accounts, not Membership Types.
Route 1: Create a flexible membership type
Route 1 actor: Golf club admin or membership staff user
Route 1 preconditions: The club has Memberships access.; Flexible Membership is enabled for the club if the Flex option is expected to be available.; The club knows the membership type name, active/inactive status, any age or service eligibility rules, and any default subscriptions.
Route 1 step 1: Open Memberships.
Route 1 step 2: Open Membership Types.
Route 1 step 3: Click CREATE MEMBERSHIP TYPE.
Route 1 step 4: In Membership Type Details, enter the Name.
Route 1 step 5: Choose Select Membership Type Status. Observed options are Active and Inactive.
Route 1 step 6: Tick Flex.
Route 1 step 7: Use Minimum Age and Maximum Age only if the type should be age-limited.
Route 1 step 8: Use Qualifying Length of Service only if eligibility depends on years of service.
Route 1 step 9: Use Next Chained Membership Type only if members should later move automatically to another type.
Route 1 step 10: In Subscription Items, use Start typing to filter available subscriptions and Select to add any default subscriptions.
Route 1 step 11: Review the Default Items table.
Route 1 step 12: Click CREATE.
Route 1 outcome: The membership type is created with Flex enabled.
Route 1 verification: Return to Membership Types.; Find the membership type row.; Confirm the Flex column shows Yes.; Open the membership type and confirm the Flex checkbox is checked and default subscription items are correct.
Route 2: Inspect or edit an existing flexible membership type
Route 2 actor: Golf club admin or membership staff user
Route 2 preconditions: The flexible membership type already exists.
Route 2 step 1: Open Memberships.
Route 2 step 2: Open Membership Types.
Route 2 step 3: Open the membership type row.
Route 2 step 4: Check Membership Type Details and confirm Flex is checked.
Route 2 step 5: Review Default Items for default subscriptions.
Route 2 step 6: Use EDIT if the membership type details need to change.
Route 2 step 7: Use the Members table on the detail view to check which members are assigned to that membership type.
Route 2 outcome: The staff user can verify or amend the flexible membership type configuration.
Route 2 verification: Return to Membership Types and confirm the row still shows the expected status and Flex value.

entries.title: Workflow family: Move a tee sheet booking
entries.content:
Use this family when the user wording is about moving, transferring, or rescheduling a tee sheet booking. Service wording such as buggy, trolley, caddie, or club hire is a variant unless observed evidence proves a separate service-specific route.
Workflow: Move a tee sheet booking
Workflow family: Move a tee sheet booking
Aliases: move a booking; reschedule a booking; transfer a booking; move a visitor booking; move a member booking; move a booking with services attached
Variant 1: Booking with attached service or hire item
Variant 1 applies when: The wording includes a buggy, trolley, caddie, club hire, or another service attached to the booking.
Variant 1 answer impact: Use the same move-booking route unless test-system evidence proves the service has a separate move workflow.
Variant 1 same workflow as: Move a tee sheet booking
Variant 2: Paid booking
Variant 2 applies when: The booking has BRS payment information attached.
Variant 2 answer impact: Use Cut from inside Booking Details so payment information remains attached, then check payment status after moving.
Route 1: Booking Details cut and paste route
Route 1 actor: Admin or staff user
Route 1 preconditions: The booking exists on the tee sheet.; The user can open Booking Details.
Route 1 step 1: Click the tee time to open the Booking Details page.
Route 1 step 2: Click Cut from inside the Booking Details page.
Route 1 step 3: Return to the tee sheet.
Route 1 step 4: Go to the new date if the booking is being moved to a different day.
Route 1 step 5: Tick the checkbox beside the target tee time.
Route 1 step 6: Click Paste.
Route 1 step 7: Check the payment status after moving the booking.
Route 1 outcome: The booking is moved while keeping payment information attached.
Route 1 verification: Check the moved booking on the target tee time.; Check payment status after the move.
Rollback policy: No write action is required to answer from this approved workflow. Future automatic write exploration must create only test records and verify rollback.

entries.title: BRS system ingestion principles
entries.content:
# BRS system ingestion principles

The BRS system crawler is used to learn reusable product behaviour, not to copy a club's private setup.

Approved knowledge includes menu structure, page purpose, setting names, product-authored help text, workflow steps, report names, filters, and relationships between areas such as tee sheet, payments, competitions, memberships, reports, and system configuration.

Do not store member names, visitor names, staff names, email addresses, phone numbers, booking references, payment amounts, green fee values, transaction identifiers, custom club policy text, or exact audit timestamps. When audit metadata is useful, record only that the product exposes last-modified information.

System knowledge must be treated as template knowledge unless it has been reviewed and approved as broadly applicable product guidance.
